messages:
sara (support): hey team, escalation from Acme: long-running SSE stream to our hosted API keeps disconnecting after ~8–12m. customer sees partial outputs (last tokens truncated) and occasional 401s on reconnect. they also report billing spikes because their client reconnect logic resends full prompt on each reconnect. :grimacing:

sara (support): repro notes from customer: python asyncio client using our streaming iterator, refresh token via oauth flow every 10m. when token refresh happens mid-stream the server returns 401, then client spawns a new connection that replays the original prompt + messages. they attached logs and an excerpt:```py
# simplified
async for chunk in client.stream_chat(session, messages):
    if chunk.type == 'event':
        print(chunk.data)

# token refresh handler runs in background and updates headers on next request
```

sara (support): they say sometimes the reconnect yields partial duplicate tokens (some tokens repeated), other times the final text is cut (like trailing clause missing). billing team flagged a 3x token charge for one session due to three reconnects in 2 minutes.

mike (sre): can you paste a raw request/response pair and request-id? also which model + region?

sara (support): request-id: rwd-req-0a1b2c3d, model: rw-ggml-13b, region: us-west-2, time window: 2026-02-27T21:10:12Z to 21:18:34Z. raw response when 401 happened:```http
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 21:15:07 GMT
X-Request-Id: rwd-req-0a1b2c3d
Content-Type: text/event-stream

event: error
data: {"code":401, "message":"token expired"}
```

anita (eng-runtime): thanks. couple thoughts: 1) we intentionally close the SSE connection on 401 to avoid serving requests with expired tokens. 2) if the client reconnects by replaying the entire prompt, they will be billed for all tokens again. server-side we don't dedupe replayed prompts unless the client uses the request-reuse header or provides a client-provided idempotency token.

anita (eng-runtime): can you confirm whether the client sets `x-client-id`/`x-idempotency-key`? also which SDK version? older py SDKs had an iterator bug where auth refresh in a background task raced with the SSE connection and could leave the iterator in an inconsistent state causing partial chunk consumption.

sara (support): they are on rwd-py-sdk 0.8.1 (installed from pip). no idempotency header set.

lee (devex): 0.8.1 rings a bell. we patched a streaming iterator race in 0.8.4 that addressed duplicate-emit + truncated-final-chunk in background-token-refresh paths. but that patch didn't change billing behavior — client replay still results in full billing. recommended immediate workaround: upgrade SDK to >=0.8.4 and set `idempotency_key` on stream start. example:```py
client.chat_stream(messages, idempotency_key=str(session_id))
```

lee (devex): also advise client to change reconnect behavior: on 401 from stream, instead of blindly replaying the whole prompt, they should: 1) attempt token refresh then 2) resume by reconciling last-seen token index (we return `last_event_id` in SSE events) or 3) request a server-side partial from cached prefix if available.

david (billing): tagging in billing: we saw a spike tied to rwd-req-0a1b2c3d and two subsequent rwd-req-0a1b2c3e/0a1b2c3f within 90s — charges were applied for each full stream since the server billed per-response tokens produced. we can offer a refund for clearly duplicated work if customer shows replay loop; need engineering confirmation that it's due to reconnect, not different queries.

anita (eng-runtime): confirming replay: logs show identical initial prompt hash for all three requests: prompt-hash: a3f5d1. That's replay. I can add a short-term mitigation: when we see a stream re-opened within 30s with identical prompt-hash and an `Authorization` header that was just refreshed, mark subsequent runs as potential-replay and attach `x-replay-suspected: true` to request metadata. Billing could use that flag to auto-review. Not a long-term dedupe but helps support triage.

sara (support): customer also reported truncated final text: anita, is that the iterator bug you mentioned? can that cut the final chunk mid-token?

anita (eng-runtime): yes, older SDK race could cause the iterator consumer to stop before draining final SSE `data: [DONE]` event if the background refresh task replaced the connection object. That leads to missing trailing tokens. server-side we still produced the final tokens; client-side lost them. upgrading the SDK should fix for them.

mike (sre): any risk the server closes long-lived streams for other reasons? network idle timeout? we usually have a 15m idle window. logs show disconnect at ~8–12m which aligns with their refresh cadence, not server idle.

lee (devex): propose action items for support to give customer: 1) upgrade py SDK >=0.8.4 (pip install --upgrade rwd-py-sdk), 2) set idempotency_key on stream calls, 3) change reconnect strategy: on 401 try renewing token and rejoin using last_event_id instead of replaying full prompt, 4) send request-ids and prompt-hash if billing review requested.

sara (support): I'll send those steps. also asked if we can hotfix SDK to avoid replaying full prompt automatically when the iterator detects a 401 — instead surface an explicit RecoverableAuthError that callers can handle. reasonable?

anita (eng-runtime): that's reasonable. for short-term we can release a 0.8.5 patch that raises RecoverableAuthError on 401 during a live stream instead of auto-reconnecting. long-term we should provide a streaming resume API that accepts last_event_id/token-index.

david (billing): I'll put a temporary hold on auto invoicing for the flagged request-ids while support gets customer logs. we can process a manual credit once we verify replay duplicates.

sara (support): customer is going to try SDK upgrade and change reconnect logic. will update here with results. thanks all. :pray:

reconnect-bot: automated note: created incident INC-2026-1843 for recurring streaming auth disconnects — assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

mike (sre): adding to oncall queue @anita, can you take a quick look at the request stream logs if needed?

anita (eng-runtime): will do, have trace for rwd-req-0a1b2c3d. initial analysis matches SDK race + token refresh closed connection. plan: emergency patch 0.8.5 + server-side 'x-replay-suspected' tag for billing.

sara (support): thanks, I'll update the customer and recommend the workaround. keeping thread open for follow-up.
